events.title: Mehrgarh Civilization
events.description: Early agricultural civilization appeared at Mehrgarh site in Balochistan, Pakistan, one of earliest Neolithic settlements in South Asia. Residents began cultivating wheat and barley, domesticating cattle and sheep.

events.title: Indus Valley Civilization (Harappan Civilization)
events.description: Highly developed urban civilization emerged in the Indus Valley, including cities like Mohenjo-daro and Harappa. Featured advanced urban planning, drainage systems, writing, and trade networks. One of the world's four great ancient civilizations.

events.title: Aryan Migration
events.description: Aryans from Central Asia migrated to Indian subcontinent, bringing Vedic culture and early Hinduism. Their language evolved into Sanskrit and modern Indo-Aryan languages.

events.title: Persian Achaemenid Empire Rule
events.description: Persian Empire conquered Indus Valley (present-day Pakistan), incorporating it into empire. Persian culture profoundly influenced this region.

events.title: Alexander's Invasion
events.description: Alexander the Great led army across Hindu Kush mountains, conquering Indus Valley. Though quickly withdrawn, brought Greek cultural influence.

events.title: Mauryan Empire Rule
events.description: Indian Mauryan Empire unified northern India, including most of present-day Pakistan. Buddhism flourished in region during Ashoka's reign.

events.title: Kushan Empire
events.description: Kushan Empire controlled present-day Pakistan and Afghanistan, promoting Silk Road trade. Gandhara art (Greco-Buddhist art) reached peak during this period.

events.title: Arab Muslim Conquest of Sindh
events.description: Arab general Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh region (present-day southern Pakistan), bringing Islam to South Asia for the first time. This marked the beginning of Islam's spread in the Indian subcontinent.

events.title: Mahmud of Ghazni's Invasions
events.description: Mahmud of Ghazni dynasty repeatedly invaded Indian subcontinent, plundering wealth and promoting Islam. Punjab became Muslim-ruled region.

events.title: Delhi Sultanate Period
events.description: Delhi Sultanate ruled northern India, including most of present-day Pakistan. Muslim rule consolidated, Islamic and Indian cultures began merging.

events.title: Mughal Empire Founded
events.description: Babur founded Mughal Empire, conquering northern India. Mughal rule would last over 300 years, profoundly influencing South Asian culture.

events.title: Akbar's Reign
events.description: Akbar expanded empire, implemented religious tolerance policies, promoted Indo-Islamic cultural fusion. Lahore became important imperial city.

events.title: Shah Jahan's Reign
events.description: Shah Jahan built Taj Mahal and many magnificent buildings in Lahore. Mughal art and architecture reached peak.

events.title: Nadir Shah's Invasion
events.description: Persia's Nadir Shah invaded India, sacking Delhi and plundering Peacock Throne. Mughal Empire began declining.

events.title: Sikh Empire
events.description: Ranjit Singh established Sikh Empire, ruling Punjab region. This was only period of Sikh independent statehood.

events.title: British Conquest of Sindh
events.description: British East India Company conquered Sindh, beginning to establish colonial rule in present-day Pakistan territory.

events.title: British Annexation of Punjab
events.description: After two Anglo-Sikh Wars, Britain annexed Punjab, entire present-day Pakistan coming under British colonial rule.

events.title: Sepoy Mutiny
events.description: Indian Rebellion broke out in northern India, including present-day Pakistan. Though suppressed, this was first major armed resistance against British colonialism.

events.title: All-India Muslim League Founded
events.description: Muslim League founded in Dhaka, advocating for Muslim political rights in British India. It later became main force for Pakistani independence.

events.title: Iqbal's Allahabad Address
events.description: Poet-philosopher Muhammad Iqbal first proposed creating independent Muslim state in northwestern India. This became ideological foundation for Pakistani independence movement.

events.title: Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution)
events.description: Muslim League passed Lahore Resolution in Lahore, formally demanding creation of independent Muslim states in India's Muslim-majority regions. This was crucial turning point in Pakistan movement.

events.title: Mountbatten Plan
events.description: British announced plan to partition India into India and Pakistan. Plan triggered mass population migrations and religious violence.

events.title: Pakistan Independence
events.description: British India partitioned, Pakistan became independent as a Muslim nation, consisting of East Pakistan (present-day Bangladesh) and West Pakistan. Muhammad Ali Jinnah became first Governor-General. August 14 became Pakistan's Independence Day.

events.title: Death of Jinnah
events.description: Pakistan's founding father Muhammad Ali Jinnah died. Pakistan lost its greatest leader, entering period of political instability.

events.title: East-West Pakistan Division
events.description: Pakistan consisted of two wings separated by 1,600 km of Indian territory. Ethnic, linguistic, and political tensions between Bengali East Pakistan and Punjabi-dominated West Pakistan grew.

events.title: First Indo-Pakistani War
events.description: India and Pakistan went to war over Kashmir. War ended with UN ceasefire, Kashmir divided into Indian and Pakistani control. Kashmir remains unresolved core dispute between two countries.

events.title: Liaquat Ali Khan Assassination
events.description: First Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated. Pakistan political situation became more turbulent.

events.title: First Constitution
events.description: Pakistan promulgated first constitution, officially becoming Islamic Republic of Pakistan. But political instability continued.

events.title: First Military Coup
events.description: General Ayub Khan launched military coup, establishing military dictatorship. This began Pakistan's long military intervention in politics history.

events.title: Second Indo-Pakistani War
events.description: India and Pakistan went to war again over Kashmir. War ended in stalemate, Kashmir issue remained unresolved.

events.title: First Democratic Election
events.description: Pakistan held first democratic election. East Pakistan's Awami League won absolute majority, but West Pakistani military refused to transfer power, triggering crisis.

events.title: Operation Searchlight and Bengali Genocide
events.description: Pakistani military launched Operation Searchlight, brutally suppressing East Pakistani people, committing genocide. About 3 million killed (mostly civilians), 200,000-400,000 women raped, 10 million refugees fled to India.

events.title: Third Indo-Pakistani War and Bangladesh Independence
events.description: India intervened, waging war against Pakistan. Pakistan defeated, East Pakistan became independent as Bangladesh. This was Pakistan's greatest humiliation and trauma.

events.title: Bhutto Government
events.description: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister, implemented nationalization and socialist policies. He promoted Pakistan's nuclear program.

events.title: Zia-ul-Haq Military Coup
events.description: General Zia-ul-Haq launched military coup, overthrowing Bhutto. Zia imposed military dictatorship for 11 years, implementing strict Islamization policies.

events.title: Bhutto Executed
events.description: Former Prime Minister Bhutto was hanged on controversial charges. This deepened Pakistan's political division.

events.title: Soviet-Afghan War
events.description: Pakistan became frontline state in Soviet-Afghan War. US provided massive aid through Pakistan to support Afghan mujahideen. Millions of Afghan refugees fled to Pakistan.

events.title: Zia Plane Crash Death
events.description: Zia-ul-Haq died in plane crash. Pakistan returned to democracy.

events.title: 'Democracy Decade'
events.description: Benazir Bhutto (Bhutto's daughter) and Nawaz Sharif alternated in power. Both governments accused of corruption, neither completed term. Military remained real power.

events.title: Nuclear Weapons Tests
events.description: Following India's nuclear tests, Pakistan conducted 6 nuclear tests, becoming the world's seventh nuclear weapons state. Indo-Pakistani nuclear standoff formed.

events.title: Kargil War
events.description: Pakistan military infiltrated Kargil region in Indian-controlled Kashmir, triggering limited war. Pakistan withdrew under international pressure, Prime Minister Sharif blamed.

events.title: Musharraf Military Coup
events.description: General Pervez Musharraf launched military coup, overthrowing Sharif government. This was Pakistan's fourth military coup.

events.title: 9/11 and War on Terror
events.description: After 9/11, US pressured Pakistan to join War on Terror. Pakistan became US ally but accused of dual-dealing, secretly supporting Taliban.

events.title: Benazir Bhutto Returns and Assassinated
events.description: Benazir Bhutto returned from exile, assassinated during campaign rally. Her Pakistan People's Party won election, her widower Zardari became president.

events.title: Mumbai Terror Attacks
events.description: Pakistan-based terrorist organization Lashkar-e-Taiba launched large-scale terror attacks in Mumbai, India, killing about 170. This severely deteriorated Indo-Pakistani relations.

events.title: Drone Strikes and Terrorism
events.description: US conducted hundreds of drone strikes in Pakistan's tribal areas. Pakistan domestic terrorist attacks frequent, thousands died. Relations with US deteriorated.

events.title: Bin Laden Killed in Pakistan
events.description: US special forces killed al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden in Abbottabad, Pakistan. Bin Laden's hideout was near Pakistan's military academy, raising international questions about whether Pakistan harbored terrorists.

events.title: Nawaz Sharif Returns to Power
events.description: Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League won election, Sharif became Prime Minister for third time. But conflicts with military persisted.

events.title: CPEC and China-Pakistan Relations
events.description: China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) launched, China investing over $60 billion in Pakistan's infrastructure. Pakistan became core node in China's Belt and Road Initiative.

events.title: Sharif Disqualified
events.description: Supreme Court disqualified Prime Minister Sharif on corruption charges. Sharif accused of military-judicial collusion.

events.title: Imran Khan Elected Prime Minister
events.description: Former cricketer Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf won election. Khan promised anti-corruption and reform.

events.title: Pulwama Attack and Air Strikes
events.description: Kashmir Pulwama terror attack killed 40 Indian soldiers. India launched air strikes on Pakistani territory, two countries on brink of war. This was most serious India-Pakistan crisis since 1999.

events.title: Khan Government Overthrown
events.description: Prime Minister Imran Khan lost no-confidence vote, removed from office. Khan accused of US-military conspiracy.

events.title: Economic Crisis
events.description: Pakistan fell into severe economic crisis, foreign reserves depleted, inflation soaring. IMF provided bailout, but economy remained fragile.

events.title: Khan Arrested
events.description: Former Prime Minister Imran Khan arrested on multiple corruption charges. Khan's supporters launched large-scale protests, attacking military facilities. Pakistan politics fell into chaos.

events.title: Economic Crisis
events.description: Pakistan faces severe economic crisis with foreign exchange shortages, soaring inflation, repeated IMF bailouts. Poverty, unemployment, and debt problems are severe.

events.title: Imran Khan Removed from Office
events.description: Parliament passed no-confidence motion, removing Imran Khan. Shehbaz Sharif (Nawaz's brother) became Prime Minister.

events.title: Imran Khan Prosecution and Arrest
events.description: Imran Khan faced multiple charges and was arrested, triggering massive protests and violent clashes by supporters. Pakistan's political crisis intensified.

events.title: Ongoing Challenges
events.description: Pakistan faces multiple challenges including economic crisis, political turmoil, terrorism, climate change (glacier melting, floods). About 40% of 240 million population lives below poverty line. Nation's future full of uncertainty.
